scenes.tts: Two neurons share one target. One starts with a tiny lead. Does the lead grow, shrink, or stay put?
scenes.visual: Title card: Why Sharing Fails. Two neurons, A and B, reach one target.
scenes.narration: Two neurons share one target. One starts with a tiny lead. Does the lead grow, shrink, or stay put?

scenes.tts: Neuron A carries a little more Track A, the receptor that binds N G F.
scenes.caption: Neuron A carries a little more TrkA, the receptor that binds NGF.
scenes.visual: Neuron A shows slightly more TrkA receptors on its axon tip than neuron B.
scenes.narration: Neuron A carries a little more TrkA, the receptor that binds NGF.

scenes.tts: Track A is a receptor tyrosine kinase. More receptor means the neuron catches more of the supply.
scenes.caption: TrkA is a receptor tyrosine kinase. More receptor means the neuron catches more of the supply.
scenes.visual: Label: TrkA, a receptor tyrosine kinase. NGF dots bind A slightly more often.
scenes.narration: TrkA is a receptor tyrosine kinase. More receptor means the neuron catches more of the supply.

scenes.tts: By chance, A catches fifty-two percent of the N G F. Neuron B catches the rest.
scenes.caption: By chance, A catches 52 percent of the NGF. Neuron B catches the rest.
scenes.visual: A pie chart: A 52 percent, B 48 percent.
scenes.narration: By chance, A catches 52 percent of the NGF. Neuron B catches the rest.

scenes.tts: Now add feedback on receptor level. Each neuron makes Track A in proportion to the N G F it catches.
scenes.caption: Now add feedback on receptor level. Each neuron makes TrkA in proportion to the NGF it catches.
scenes.visual: An arrow loops from NGF caught back to TrkA made, on each neuron.
scenes.narration: Now add feedback on receptor level. Each neuron makes TrkA in proportion to the NGF it catches.

scenes.tts: And each neuron's catch is simply proportional to its Track A.
scenes.caption: And each neuron's catch is simply proportional to its TrkA.
scenes.visual: Label beside the pie: share follows TrkA.
scenes.narration: And each neuron's catch is simply proportional to its TrkA.

scenes.tts: Both neurons now make more receptor. But B grows by the same fraction as A.
scenes.visual: Both receptor bars grow by the same fraction. The pie updates: still 52 to 48.
scenes.narration: Both neurons now make more receptor. But B grows by the same fraction as A.

scenes.tts: After many rounds, what share does neuron A hold?
scenes.visual: On screen: after many rounds, A's share is ...? Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: After many rounds, what share does neuron A hold?

scenes.tts: Still fifty-two percent. Proportional sharing keeps the ratio fixed, round after round.
scenes.caption: Still 52 percent. Proportional sharing keeps the ratio fixed, round after round.
scenes.visual: The pie updates six times and never changes. Row of numbers: 52, 52, 52, 52, 52, 52 percent.
scenes.narration: Still 52 percent. Proportional sharing keeps the ratio fixed, round after round.

scenes.tts: Each neuron's gain is a fixed fraction of what it already has.
scenes.visual: Two bars grow side by side, keeping the same ratio.
scenes.narration: Each neuron's gain is a fixed fraction of what it already has.

scenes.tts: Add some steady basal synthesis of Track A. Both neurons get the same top-up, so the shares drift back toward even.
scenes.caption: Add some steady basal synthesis of TrkA. Both neurons get the same top-up, so the shares drift back toward even.
scenes.visual: A basal trickle feeds both neurons equally; the pie drifts toward an even split.
scenes.narration: Add some steady basal synthesis of TrkA. Both neurons get the same top-up, so the shares drift back toward even.

scenes.tts: So in this setup, feedback on receptor level alone does not make a winner.
scenes.visual: A card: in this setup, level feedback alone does not make a winner.
scenes.narration: So in this setup, feedback on receptor level alone does not make a winner.

scenes.tts: Now let N G F do two things at once. It raises Track A, so the neuron catches more.
scenes.caption: Now let NGF do two things at once. It raises TrkA, so the neuron catches more.
scenes.visual: First arrow from NGF to more TrkA receptors.
scenes.narration: Now let NGF do two things at once. It raises TrkA, so the neuron catches more.

scenes.tts: It also lengthens each signal, so every caught molecule counts for longer.
scenes.visual: Second arrow from NGF to a signal timer that runs longer.
scenes.narration: It also lengthens each signal, so every caught molecule counts for longer.

scenes.tts: For simple arithmetic, assume each signal lasts in proportion to the catch. And Track A is made in proportion to the signal. Then each round squares the ratio of A to B.
scenes.caption: For simple arithmetic, assume each signal lasts in proportion to the catch. And TrkA is made in proportion to the signal. Then each round squares the ratio of A to B.
scenes.visual: Label: signal = catch times duration, an assumed toy update. The ratio between A and B squares each round.
scenes.narration: For simple arithmetic, assume each signal lasts in proportion to the catch. And TrkA is made in proportion to the signal. Then each round squares the ratio of A to B.

scenes.tts: Watch A's share climb, round after round, until it holds almost all of it.
scenes.visual: The pie updates six rounds: 52, 54, 58, 65, 78, 93 percent. Note: assumed toy update and teaching rounds, not measured biology or time.
scenes.narration: Watch A's share climb, round after round, until it holds almost all of it.

scenes.tts: The lead feeds itself. That is positive feedback, the loop you met in signaling circuits.
scenes.visual: A loop arrow labelled positive feedback, with a small link to the signaling circuits lesson.
scenes.narration: The lead feeds itself. That is positive feedback, the loop you met in signaling circuits.

scenes.tts: Here is the condition it needs. A lead can grow only when the reward rises faster than the lead.
scenes.visual: A card: a lead can grow only when the reward rises faster than the lead.
scenes.narration: Here is the condition it needs. A lead can grow only when the reward rises faster than the lead.

scenes.tts: What about arriving first? Arriving first may well give a neuron its small lead.
scenes.visual: An axon reaching the target slightly ahead of another. Label: may give the lead.
scenes.narration: What about arriving first? Arriving first may well give a neuron its small lead.

scenes.tts: Arrival order alone cannot explain how a small lead grows while the supply keeps coming.
scenes.visual: The early axon's lead stays small under proportional sharing.
scenes.narration: Arrival order alone cannot explain how a small lead grows while the supply keeps coming.

scenes.tts: And the target keeps releasing N G F throughout the death period, not just at first.
scenes.caption: And the target keeps releasing NGF throughout the death period, not just at first.
scenes.visual: NGF dots keep flowing from the target across a time bar labelled death period.
scenes.narration: And the target keeps releasing NGF throughout the death period, not just at first.

scenes.tts: The simulation in the lesson splits its neurons another way. Its Track A response to each neuron's share is switch-like.
scenes.caption: The simulation in the lesson splits its neurons another way. Its TrkA response to each neuron's share is switch-like.
scenes.visual: A sketch of the simulation: twelve bars, and a steep S-shaped curve labelled switch-like response to share.
scenes.narration: The simulation in the lesson splits its neurons another way. Its TrkA response to each neuron's share is switch-like.

scenes.tts: Takeaway. For identical neurons with proportional sharing and no basal synthesis, a lead stays frozen. To grow, the reward has to rise faster than the lead.
scenes.visual: End card: identical neurons, proportional sharing, no basal synthesis: a lead stays frozen. To grow, the reward must rise faster than the lead.
scenes.narration: Takeaway. For identical neurons with proportional sharing and no basal synthesis, a lead stays frozen. To grow, the reward has to rise faster than the lead.
